newsitem.title: USA: Clintonite got campaign check in White House - NBC.
newsitem.headline: Clintonite got campaign check in White House - NBC.

text.p: Hillary Rodham Clinton's chief of staff accepted a $50,000 political donation at the White House in 1995, which according to a former prosecutor was a violation of federal law, NBC News reported on Wednesday.

The network said Maggie Williams, Mrs Clinton's top aide, received the money from California businessman Johnny Chung, who gave her a $50,000 check made payable to the Democratic National Committee on March 9, 1995.

It said the White House acknowledged that Chung had given Williams the check after he and six Chinese officials had their picture taken with the first lady, and it quoted White House spokeswoman Ann Lewis as saying it was legal and proper for Williams to accept the donation.

"The act of handling and forwarding the contribution does not violate the Hatch Act" which bars federal employees from engaging in political activity, Ann Lewis, deputy White House communications director, told NBC.
However, the network quoted former Republican U.S. Attorney Joseph DiGenova as saying the act was illegal.
"The White House is completely wrong. It is totally improper. It is illegal to receive federal campaign funds on property at the White House or at the Executive Office Building," DiGenova said.
The report is likely to add fuel to the campaign financing controversy that has hounded President Clinton since before his reelection last Nov. 5.

Chung, who was described as a "hustler"in a memo written by a National Security Council aide, has been implicated in other facets of the burgeoning controversy. The Democratic National Committee has returned more than $1.5 million in questionable contributions raised by him and two other Chinese-American men.
